messages.content: Write a monthly engineering update for a team of twelve, covering a migration, two hires, and a slipped deadline. Around 200 words.

Engineering Update — August 2026

The database migration finished last week. We moved the primary datastore off the old cluster without downtime.

The team spent the back half of the month watching dashboards and fixing the query patterns that didn't translate cleanly. Thanks to everyone who took an on-call shift during the cutover. Two new engineers joined us this month: Priya Nair on the platform team and Marcus Webb on infrastructure. Both are ramping up on the codebase now — say hello if you haven't already, and pair with them where you can.

On the downside, the reporting API redesign is not shipping this month. We underestimated how much the migration work would eat into the sprint, and the two overlapped more than planned.

The new target is mid-October. If your team depends on the new endpoints, expect the current API to stay stable until then — no breaking changes are coming before the new release. It was a lot to get through this month, between the infrastructure change, the two new hires, and the pushed deadline. Priorities for September are stabilizing the new database setup, getting Priya and Marcus fully ramped, and restarting the reporting API work with a more realistic timeline.
The deadline slipped again. Update it and explain why.

The database migration finished last week. We moved the primary datastore off the old cluster without downtime.

The team spent the back half of the month watching dashboards and fixing the query patterns that didn't translate cleanly. Thanks to everyone who took an on-call shift during the cutover. Two new engineers joined us this month: Priya Nair on the platform team and Marcus Webb on infrastructure. Both are ramping up on the codebase now — say hello if you haven't already, and pair with them where you can.

The reporting API redesign has slipped again, this time to late November. We restarted the work in September on what we thought was a realistic timeline, but the migration's aftermath took longer to settle than expected: query patterns kept surfacing through the first two weeks, and that ate the runway we'd set aside for the redesign. Rather than compress the remaining work into a tight window and repeat the same mistake, we're pushing the date out and giving it room.

If your team depends on the new endpoints, the current API stays stable until then. No breaking changes are coming before the new release.

Priorities for the rest of the fall: keep the database setup stable, finish ramping Priya and Marcus, and get the reporting API redesign properly underway with a buffer built in this time.
